description: Single-panel mechanical-property plot, labelled "Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC" in the upper left and corresponding to Fig. 28(b). Composition is on the x-axis, C (wt%), from 0 to 2. There are two ordinates: left, Strength (MPa), roughly 300 to 1300; right, "TE or δ (%)", 0 to 100. Five series are overlaid. UTS (magenta filled squares) rises steadily from ~770 MPa at C≈0.3 to ~1250 MPa at C≈1.8. YS (dark-blue filled diamonds) dips slightly to a shallow minimum near C≈0.7 (near the 500-600 MPa region) then climbs steeply to ~1250 MPa at C≈1.8. TE (black filled triangles) rises from near 0 at C≈0.3 to a peak of about 60% at C≈1.1 before falling to ~10% at C≈1.8. A red asterisk-marked δ curve decreases from ~85% at C≈0.3 to zero near C≈1.0-1.1. A second red asterisk series labelled κ sits near zero at C≈1.5-1.9. The point where δ reaches zero and TE peaks defines the duplex-to-single-phase-austenite transition; beyond it, strength continues to rise while elongation drops, consistent with κ-carbide formation in austenite. The caption states data come from Refs. [8,11,63,73,77,78,160] and that the figure covers two Mn series, (a) Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC and (b) Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC.

observations.observation: The panel is labelled "Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC" in the upper-left corner, identifying it as the Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC series.
The x-axis is C (wt%) from 0 to 2; the left ordinate is Strength (MPa) and the right ordinate is "TE or δ (%)" from 0 to 100.
UTS (magenta filled squares) increases monotonically with C, from about 770 MPa at C≈0.3 to about 1250 MPa at C≈1.8.
YS (dark-blue filled diamonds) shows a shallow minimum around C≈0.7 before rising steeply to about 1250 MPa at C≈1.8.
TE (black filled triangles) rises to a maximum of roughly 60% at C≈1.1 and then decreases to about 10% at C≈1.8.
The red asterisk-marked δ curve declines from about 85% at C≈0.3 to zero near C≈1.0-1.1.
A second red asterisk series labelled κ lies near zero at high C (≈1.5-1.9), annotated with the κ label and an arrow.
For Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC steels, single-phase austenite is reached when C reaches about 1.0%.
For single-phase austenitic steels the strength increases but the elongation decreases with increasing C, attributed to increased κ-carbide precipitation or ordering in the austenite.
The caption states the figure shows tensile properties of two Fe-Mn-Al-C series, (a) Fe-30Mn-9Al-xC and (b) Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC.
The caption states the data are taken from Refs. [8,11,63,73,77,78,160].

subfigures.description: Plot of Strength (MPa) versus C (wt%) for Fe-20Mn-10Al-xC steel with overlaid UTS (magenta squares), YS (blue diamonds), TE (black triangles), δ-ferrite (red asterisks) and κ-carbide (red asterisks) series. The δ fraction falls to zero near C≈1.0-1.1 where TE peaks; UTS and YS rise steeply at high C while TE drops.
